subject: Dedicated reservation scenarios & onramp template — VerdantAI
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Ava Johnson <ava.j@verdant.ai>, Luis Moreno <luis.m@verdant.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated reservation scenarios & onramp template — VerdantAI

Hi Ava / Luis,

Thanks for the time this morning. Per our call, attached is a compact set of reservation options to fit VerdantAI's usage profile across proof-of-concept and production ramp. I put three clear pathways so you can pick trade-offs for cost vs. throughput predictability. See the attached spreadsheet (verdantai_reservation_options.xlsx) for the numeric breakdown; summary below.

Quick summary (all options assume Redwood tuning for model batching and KV cache):

1) Option A — Pilot (low commitment)
- Minimum reserved: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (shared pool)
- Ramp: month 0: 4 engaged (allocation policy: on-demand burst to 8), month 1–3: scale to 8, month 4+: evaluation for step-up
- Use case: customer-facing POC, <10 reqs/s steady, occasional spikes to 25 reqs/s
- SLA: no hard SLA; 99% best-effort latency target included in plan

2) Option B — Steady baseline (recommended for start of production)
- Minimum reserved: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated lane)
- Ramp: month 0: activate 8 (canary), month 1: 16, month 2: 24; full activation by month 3
- Canary & canary-to-prod window: first 2 weeks on a canary subset of traffic with automatic fallback to hosted models
- Cost smoothing: 6-month smoothing credit applied on commit

3) Option C — Predictable throughput (enterprise commit)
- Minimum reserved: 64 A100-eq GPUs with 20% buffer pool for peak bursts
- Ramp: tranche-based (25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%) over 4 quarters; optional geo-burst routing to EU region for DR
- SLA: 99.9% uptime for dedicated lane, tail-latency SLOs defined in SOW

Key operational notes:
- Autoscaling policy options: fixed minimum + burst pool, or predictive autoscale based on 24-hr rolling traffic
- Caching: We recommend enabling prefix caching for interactive flows. It reduces token cost by ~18–25% for your sample traces.
- Quantization profile: For the LLM family you described (40B variants), a mixed-int8 path gives best cost/latency balance; we included quantization impact estimates in the spreadsheet.

Next steps I propose: pick a preferred option (A/B/C) and whether you want a 3- or 12-month committed cadence. Once decided, we’ll produce a short SOW and a DocuSign to lock capacity and start onboarding. I’ve attached a draft SOW (SOW_draft_v1.pdf) for option B as a starting point.

If you want, Ben and Marissa can run a quick throughput run next week against a sanitized prompt set to validate the projected req/s per GPU.

Thanks,
Grace
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: verdantai_reservation_options.xlsx (spreadsheet — 3 sheets: summary, monthly burn, quantization-impact)
Attachment: SOW_draft_v1.pdf (draft SOW — payment terms placeholder)
From: Ava Johnson <ava.j@verdant.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Luis Moreno <luis.m@verdant.ai>, salesops@verdant.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation scenarios & onramp template — VerdantAI

Thanks Grace, this is helpful. A few quick clarifying questions before we choose a path: 

1) For Option B ramp cadence — can you guarantee capacity for the canary period (we can't afford dropped traffic during that first 2 weeks)? Would the canary run on isolated GPU Lanes or share the pool with other tenants?

2) For Option C — what does the 20% buffer pool look like operationally? Is that pre-reserved or a burst allowance billed on use?

3) SOC2 evidence and audit logs — we need explicit confirmation we can receive per-token audit log exports and an SOC2 attestation pdf before we sign a 12-month commit. Do you have that on hand?

Also, curious if you can show a concrete cost comparison using our sample daily QPS of 120k tokens/day (spread over 24 hours). The spreadsheet has projections but we want to be sure the math matches.

Best,
Ava
VP Product
VerdantAI

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027, at 09:18, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com> wrote:
> (original message quoted)
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2027 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation scenarios & onramp template — VerdantAI

Grace / Marissa —

Ava's questions are standard. Quick answers for us to confirm before responding:
- Canary capacity: we can reserve an isolated lane for canaries (billing as part of initial activation). If Verdant wants the strictest isolation for the two-week canary, suggest we charge a transient canary surcharge (~10% of month-1 burn) to reserve the lane resources.
- Buffer pool: for Option C we typically structure the buffer as pre-reserved GPUs in the pool (not billed as usage) so latency SLOs can be honored — customers prefer this for mission-critical apps. We can offer an alternative where buffer is a billed burst with a higher per-hour rate, but that weakens the strict SLO guarantee.
- SOC2 + logs: operations can export per-request metadata (timestamp, model, request_id, token count) as CSVs and we have an SOC2 attestation PDF (2026 report) we can share. Marissa, can you attach the SOC2 bundle to the reply?

If we make Option B the default, we should also consider a 90-day ramp review clause that allows Verdant to accelerate to Option C at pre-defined volume milestones. That helps them start with lower commit while giving us a clear path to expand.

Ben
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: soc2_evidence_summary.zip (contains SOC2 attestation PDF, control matrix, sample_log.csv)

On the cost numbers: Grace, Ben — I've run the spreadsheet for Verdant's ~120k tokens/day sample. For Option B with a 24-GPU steady baseline, the effective net token cost after 6-month smoothing and expected caching is ~0.00085 $/token surface (spreadsheet shows monthly burn). I included a scenario tab with the canary surcharge factored in.

Ava — if you want, we can schedule a 60-minute throughput run next Tue to validate tokens/sec per GPU. We will use a sanitized trace and return full profiling (latency percentiles, warm-cache vs cold-cache).

Marissa
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Ava Johnson <ava.j@verdant.ai>

Date: Thu, 4 Nov 2027 10:11:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation scenarios & onramp template — VerdantAI

Thanks all — the SOC2 bundle looks good. We want to proceed with Option B but with the following modifications:

- Start with a 3-month pilot commit for 24 GPUs with the 2-week isolated canary (we accept the transient canary surcharge).
- Include a 90-day ramp review clause with explicit volume milestones to accelerate to a 12-month 64-GPU (Option C) commit if milestones are met.
- We need the per-request audit export to be pushed to our S3 daily (s3://verdantai-audit/requests/) in addition to the download link. Please include the delivery pipeline in the SOW.

Please prepare the SOW and DocuSign for the pilot commit and share pricing with the canary surcharge and the 90-day milestone language.

Best,
Ava
VP Product, VerdantAI
